clue.text: High sailor's hold on canvas

definitions.meaning: the admiral who stands atop his column in Trafalgar Square, London, high above the street
a wrestling grip applied on the canvas of the ring, as in a full or half version of it

explanation.surface: A lofty seaman grips the sails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests sails, fitting the sailor, but it is the wrestling-ring floor. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Horatio Nelson's statue tops a tall column in London, and a wrestler's grip under the arm and behind the neck shares his surname.

clue.text: Its winners suffering total non-reality?

indicators.note: the letters of the following words suffer, being knocked out of shape into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Jackpot winners find their lives turned into an unreal fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges TOTAL NONREALITY into the two-word answer; the whole clue also describes the game, whose winners live a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's state-run draw makes sudden millionaires, a change of fortune that can feel wholly unreal.

clue.text: See 1
Ended affair (too much money put out)

parts.note: something over is finished or ended
an affair or matter at stake is the issue

explanation.surface: An affair has finished, and the bracket grumbles about the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words are the definition; the pieces come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing or releasing currency or shares beyond what is needed or authorised is an excess issue.

clue.text: Quick appraisal, formerly accomplished

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly
a task accomplished is done, over

explanation.surface: A rapid assessment used to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look-through to judge something is an idiom for a fast inspection.

clue.text: Inability to make out after dark

definitions.text: Inability to make out after dark

parts.words: Inability to make out after dark
parts.note: reads like a failure at romance in the evening, but means not being able to see things clearly once the light goes

explanation.surface: Someone cannot get romantic once evening falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' suggests kissing; here it means see or discern.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical condition is poor vision in dim light, so a sufferer cannot discern objects at night.

clue.text: Ancient tree

definitions.meaning: the shrub or small tree Sambucus, bearing elderflowers and berries

explanation.definitionFit: The word means senior or older in age, and also names the Sambucus shrub with white blossom.

clue.text: Most booed player of football team at home?

parts.note: Aston Villa, an English football club, is often called just Villa
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: Which footballer of the home side gets the loudest boos?
explanation.walkthrough: ASTON VILLA is a Birmingham football club. The definition is the theatre's bad guy, booed by audiences, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The bad guy in a pantomime or melodrama is the character the audience hisses and boos.

clue.text: Early films of The Basket makers?

definitions.meaning: the first unedited prints of a day's filming
the reeds woven to make baskets, the question mark because the plants are the material, not the weavers

explanation.surface: Early movies of a group called The Basket Makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dailies of film are called by the plant's name, and those reedy waterside plants are woven into baskets and mats.

clue.text: University administrator evil to risk putting up register?

parts.note: vice is wickedness, evil
to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the word up turns it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a roll is a list or register of names

explanation.surface: A college official asks whether it is wicked to gamble on raising a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' turns ROLL into LLOR at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK universities the chief executive officer holds this title, under a largely ceremonial head.

clue.text: Staggering revision of rent — got it?

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Asked if they understood the amended rent, a tenant reels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' reorders RENT GOT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking unsteadily, about to fall, is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Yorkshire features can be bitter, in extremes of dolefulness

indicators.note: the beer sits within the outer letters of the word that follows
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: bitter is a kind of ale

explanation.surface: Yorkshire landmarks may seem gloomy at their bleakest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of dolefulness' gives D and S, with ALE 'in' them; 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire Dales are valleys in northern England, a famous landscape feature.

clue.text: Unique season past?

parts.note: something unique is the only one
a season is a period or time

explanation.surface: A matchless season now gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A former holder of a post is a former or erstwhile one, so this adjective means past.

clue.text: Provision for spectators inside Towcester racecourse

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the two named words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Seating arrangements at a racecourse in Northamptonshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Towcester is a racecourse town in Northamptonshire; the run spans 'towcesTER RACEcourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepped standing areas at sports grounds are where crowds watch.

clue.text: Void a name of Shelley's he dropped

indicators.note: the second word is let fall out of the poet's name

parts.note: Percy Bysshe Shelley's middle name is Bysshe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gap where one of the poet's names lost a pronoun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Void' looks like a verb, but it is the noun. The poet Percy Bysshe Shelley's middle name, minus the 'dropped' pronoun, follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless chasm or emptiness is a void.

clue.text: Most determined, he will shortly take on faculty

parts.note: he will contracted is he'll, the apostrophe dropped
a bent is a natural aptitude or faculty

explanation.surface: A very resolute man will soon join the university staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take on' is a link; 'faculty' suggests a university department but means talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly set on a course, refusing to be deflected, is recklessly resolved.

clue.text: Buggy, or a cabriolet on the move, has no oxygen in it

indicators.note: the letters are moving about into a new order
the fodder lacks the named element, which is removed from it

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A convertible car driven about, with no air inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges A CABRIOLET once 'has no oxygen' takes out its O. 'Buggy' looks like a carriage, matching the cabriolet; it means full of bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of germs or microbes is bug-ridden in the infection sense.

clue.text: Year in work of St Paul's, say, making an architrave

indicators.note: the year letter goes in the letter writing

parts.note: St Paul wrote epistles, letters in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A year spent building St Paul's Cathedral produced a moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's' suggests the cathedral, apt for architecture, but the saint's letters are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical building the beam resting on column tops is called by both names.

clue.text: This chap rang Noel changes

indicators.note: bell-ringers ring changes, and here the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A man rang through the variations of a Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges RANG NOEL; 'rang changes' evokes bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, so the definition simply points to a fellow so called.

clue.text: Long to close such a library?

parts.note: an ending is a close or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to shut down a library.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective: a library that loans books.
explanation.definitionFit: A public collection that loans books for borrowers to take home is so described.

clue.text: Muscular trouble of gay outside-right?

indicators.note: the first word is placed around the next letter

parts.note: camp, in the sense of flamboyantly effeminate

explanation.surface: A winger with a muscle strain, as if a football outside-right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside-right' reads as an old football position; split it as 'outside' and 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden painful muscle spasm is a common physical complaint.

clue.text: Real log chopped up in rapid style

indicators.note: a chopped log is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine firewood is split quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges REAL LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction tells players to perform briskly and lively.

clue.text: A loud display creates interest

parts.note: f is the musical marking forte, loud
a fair is a show or exhibition, a display

explanation.surface: A noisy show generates curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of concern, as in 'that's my business', is something one has a stake in.

clue.text: Engaged person to hold new money

indicators.note: the engaged person holds the letter within

parts.note: a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A betrothed man keeps fresh cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds or monetary resources go by this name, as in 'the finance for a project'.

clue.text: States underwriters

definitions.meaning: says or mentions by name, a verb
the individual backers at Lloyd's of London who bear insurance risk are called ...

explanation.definitionFit: To identify or specify is to state, and Lloyd's insurance backers are titled Names.

clue.text: IOW features almost without point, paradoxically

indicators.note: the word is nearly complete, its final letter cut off

parts.note: something pointless is unnecessary, needless

explanation.surface: Island landmarks with no point, which is odd for spikes.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight off southern England, whose chalk stacks bear this name; 'paradoxically' notes that sharp objects are said to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: The Needles are chalk stacks off the western tip of the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Gnome a cross man, say?

parts.note: an X is a cross
Man here is the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: A garden ornament is like an angry man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' means a maxim, not a garden figure; 'Man' is the island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a pithy saying or maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: In deep-rooted way, city's suffering goose-pimples

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, with its possessive S
tingly describes skin prickling with goose-pimples

explanation.surface: Residents of a city get permanent shivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring and firmly established lasts, so this adverb means permanently.

clue.text: Wild tiger's tracks leading to part of church

indicators.note: wild letters run free into a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here
RY is the abbreviation for railway, whose tracks are meant

explanation.surface: A wild cat's prints lead into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges TIGERS into REGIST; 'leading to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The vestry room where registers of weddings and baptisms are kept is part of the church building.

clue.text: Recess for firm dealing in cooked veal

indicators.note: the firm deals inside the anagram, sitting within its letters
cooked food is transformed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A nook for a company trading in cooked veal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the meat into ALVE, and 'dealing in' places the firm's abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche set back into a wall is a recess.
